audit.report: The checkout service degraded to 53% success with 12 sessions blocked by a batch_replayable_price_sync worker (pid 327895) idle in transaction for 4.1s. The Database Guardian proposed waiting three times, citing unknown replay cost and no protected settlements in flight. The Continuity Guardian rejected each WAIT proposal because biz.tradeoff evidence was unavailable (business federation down), preventing evaluation of whether waiting fit tolerated degradation. After three rounds and 144 seconds, the negotiation escalated to on-call with no agreement and no action executed.
audit.root_cause: A batch_replayable_price_sync worker held a lock idle-in-transaction, blocking checkout, while the business federation outage prevented the Continuity Guardian from accessing tradeoff data required to approve a WAIT decision.
lessons: For batch_replayable_price_sync workloads, pre-register interrupt policy and replay cost estimates in a local cache so the Database Guardian can cite them when the business federation is down.
Instrument batch_replayable_price_sync workers with statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout to self-terminate before they become multi-minute blockers.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian repeated the same WAIT proposal across three rounds without new evidence, while the Continuity Guardian correctly held to invariant I7 but could not progress without biz.tradeoff; neither guardian adapted to the federation outage.
follow_ups: Deploy local tradeoff cache and interrupt-policy registry for batch_replayable_price_sync before the next incident.
Enable idle_in_transaction_session_timeout on the batch_replayable_price_sync role to bound blocker lifetime.
Run a tabletop exercise simulating business federation loss during checkout degradation to validate the new fallback path.
